summary: TestValidateServiceResponseCoversCatalog restores its coverage bit only one way — latent stub leak if catalog ever enters the smoke gate
description:
Incidental finding from TKT-95's ai-review pass (deferred there, not fixed — it is
outside that diff's scope).

`smoke/contract_validation_catalog_test.go`'s `TestValidateServiceResponseCoversCatalog`
snapshots `smokeCoverage["catalog listPublicVenues"]`, deletes it, drives a synthetic
(stack-free) response through `validateServiceResponse`, and then restores the bit **only
when it had previously been set**:

```go
defer func() {
    if prior {
        smokeCoverageMu.Lock()
        smokeCoverage[op] = true
        smokeCoverageMu.Unlock()
    }
}()
```

When `prior` was false, the synthetic response's coverage bit **survives in the global
map**. Today that is harmless: catalog is deliberately absent from
`smokeCoverageGatedServices` (ADR-030), so `uncovered2xxOps()` never reads a catalog key
and nothing consumes the leaked bit.

It stops being harmless the moment catalog enters the smoke gate — i.e. the recorded
ADR-030 amendment ticket. At that point `listPublicVenues` would count as covered on the
strength of a hand-built `{"venues":[]}` literal, defeating the gate's real-handler /
real-store claim for that operation.

TKT-95 hit the identical shape in a *gated* service (it copied this pattern into
`TestConcurrentPostValidatesAndRecordsCoverage`, where the operation is
`inventory createHold` and inventory **is** gated). The adversarial review caught it as a
high finding; the fix there restores both ways and adds a `t.Cleanup` guard that asserts
its own cleanup, mutation-checked.

## Conditions of Success
- `TestValidateServiceResponseCoversCatalog` restores the exact prior state both ways
  (`delete` when `prior` was false).
- It carries the same self-asserting cleanup guard as
  `TestConcurrentPostValidatesAndRecordsCoverage`, so a future one-way revert fails a test
  rather than sitting latent.
- `make check` passes.

## Notes
- Trivially small and test-only, hence `risk:low`. The reason it is a ticket at all rather
  than a direct commit is that it is product-test code with a real (if currently dormant)
  correctness claim behind it.
- **Do this before the ADR-030 catalog-gate-flip ticket**, not after — the flip is what
  makes the latent leak live. Worth a `blocks` link once that ticket exists.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Filed from TKT-95's ai-review triage (incidental)

Verified at HEAD before filing: the one-way restore is at
`smoke/contract_validation_catalog_test.go`, and `smokeCoverageGatedServices` in
`smoke/coverage_test.go` is `["inventory","commerce","payments","access"]` — catalog absent,
which is exactly why the leak is currently inert.

Not fixed inside TKT-95: that PR's diff is the helper unification plus the five catalog
happy-paths, and fixing an adjacent test's dormant defect there would have been scope
creep on a PR the review pass had already converged on. Filing rather than fixing is the
triage rule (`quality-practices.md` §2 — incidental findings become Backlog issues, never
silent drops).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness - PASS

Shaped at claim time rather than earlier: this ticket was born from TKT-95's ai-review triage and
filed straight to Backlog with a description but no `readiness` object and no context-memo. Both are
now on the ticket. Verified against HEAD `61629eae`, not against the filing comment.

| DoR item | State | Note |
|---|---|---|
| objective | met | One-way restore leaks a stub-satisfied coverage bit; inert today, live at the ADR-030 flip. |
| scope | met | One test function in one file. No production code, no change to the gate's scope. |
| uncertainties | met | None material - the pattern to copy is committed in-repo. |

| approach | met | Mirror the committed TKT-95 shape: both-ways restore + self-asserting `t.Cleanup`. |
| first_slice | met | The ticket *is* the slice. |
| success | met | The three COS as written on the description. |
| context_memo | met | Baked; `governingAdrs` = ADR-030, ADR-028, both `git cat-file -e` verified at HEAD. |

**Re-verified at HEAD (not taken from the filing comment):**
- `smoke/contract_validation_catalog_test.go:56-62` still carries the one-way `if prior` defer.
- `smokeCoverageGatedServices` is still `["inventory","commerce","payments","access"]`
  (`smoke/coverage_test.go:90`) - catalog absent, so the leaked bit is still unconsumed.
- The reference implementation exists at `smoke/contract_validation_test.go:318-343`, both-ways
  restore plus the `t.Cleanup` leak assertion.
- No ADR-030-amendment / catalog-gate-flip ticket exists on the board yet, so the `blocks` link the
  description asks for cannot be wired now. Recorded here instead: whoever files that ticket should
  link it `blocked-by TKT-140`.

**Concerns:** none.

**Verdict: PASS.** Scope is one test function, the target pattern is committed and reviewed, and the
governing ADR (ADR-030) constrains the fix *away* from the tempting wrong answer (adding catalog to
the gate) rather than leaving it open.

objective.note: TestValidateServiceResponseCoversCatalog restores its smokeCoverage bit only when prior was true, so a false-prior run leaks a stub-satisfied bit into the global map. Inert today (catalog absent from smokeCoverageGatedServices, ADR-030) but live the moment catalog enters the gate.

scope.note: IN: smoke/contract_validation_catalog_test.go only - two-way restore + self-asserting t.Cleanup guard mirroring TestConcurrentPostValidatesAndRecordsCoverage. OUT: any change to smokeCoverageGatedServices, ADR-030's scope, or the catalog gate flip itself; no production code.

uncertainties.note: None material. The pattern to copy is committed in-repo at smoke/contract_validation_test.go:318-343; the sequential-execution assumption (no t.Parallel in smoke) is already documented in the test's own header comment and unchanged.

dependencies.note: Zero open blockers. Only link is found-in TKT-95 (merged, informational, not a blocker). The ADR-030 catalog-gate-flip ticket does not exist yet, so no blocks link can be wired; the description records that this must land first.

approach.note: Copy the committed TKT-95 shape: replace the `if prior` defer with a both-ways restore (set when prior, delete when not) and add a t.Cleanup that asserts the restore happened. Test-only; not auth/money/migration/CI, so the deferred-exception rule does not apply.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice - a single test function in a single file. Nothing to split.

success.note: The three COS on the description: two-way restore, self-asserting cleanup guard matching the TKT-95 reference, make check green.

context_memo.note: Baked below on the ticket's context object; governingAdrs re-resolved against docs/adr/ at HEAD 61629eae (ADR-030 and ADR-028 both cat-file verified).

governingAdrs.why: Catalog is deliberately OUT of the smoke happy-path coverage gate (smokeCoverageGatedServices = inventory, commerce, payments, access). This is what makes the leak inert today and what must NOT be changed by this ticket - do not 'fix' the leak by adding catalog to the gate, and do not weaken TestCatalogCoverageGateIsDeliberatelyUnitScoped, which pins that list exactly and in order.

Response-contract drift fails closed - validateServiceResponse Fatals on a body that does not match the committed contract, which is why the synthetic {"venues":[]} fixture must stay spec-valid. Any change to the fixture body is a contract question, not a test-style question.

reference.summary: The exact pattern to mirror: both-ways restore + self-asserting t.Cleanup, as landed by TKT-95 for the gated-service twin of this test.
The test under repair, with the one-way `if prior` defer.
